whatContradictsTheRepository.what: The registry asserts Forms 1 and 3 are HELD at Nationwide paths that this checkout cannot corroborate.
whatContradictsTheRepository.detail: Both carry sourceState CURRENTNESS_UNVERIFIED — the state that means the corpus already holds matching bytes — against paths under private/Nationwide Record Clearing/LegalEase Iowa/forms/. That tree is not mounted in this session, and the committed corpus index holds exactly four IA rows, all of them Rule 2.86 Form 4 or Form 5 across two custodies. Neither Form 1 nor Form 3 appears in it at any path or hash.
whatContradictsTheRepository.whyThisMatters: CURRENTNESS_UNVERIFIED tells a downstream lane the document is in hand and only its edition is in question. For anything reading this checkout, it is not in hand. A source falsely called held suppresses the acquisition of a real gap — which is the exact failure mode the admission rule exists to prevent.
whatContradictsTheRepository.notAnAccusation: The Nationwide custody may genuinely hold them. The claim is unverifiable here, not disproven, and the registry does not distinguish the two.

whatContradictsTheRepository.what: The repository holds records of two different editions of Rule 2.86 Form 1 and Form 3, and the compiled runtime profile was built from the older ones.
whatContradictsTheRepository.detail: The profile's source.references pin Form 1 at sha256 983d1375… (292048 bytes), Form 2 at df3380d9… (331574 bytes) and Form 3 at d8f958c1… (287801 bytes), all from LegalEase Iowa/. The manifest and registry pin Form 1 at d3e68933… (268162 bytes) and Form 3 at 6f222685… (263607 bytes). Same forms by their printed faces; different files. The profile also names 01_29_2021_order_chapter_2.pdf, the January 2021 supervisory order, as its controlling reference.
whatContradictsTheRepository.whyThisMatters: The Iowa runtime's rules and copy were compiled from an edition that is not the edition the acquisition conveyor pins for the packet. If an overlay is later built against the pinned bytes while the runtime's question flow came from the 2021 text, the two can disagree about the form's items without anything flagging it.
whatContradictsTheRepository.whatItIsNot: Not a defect I can adjudicate. It is a currentness and version-alignment question for whoever owns the Iowa profile.

whatContradictsTheRepository.what: The registry locates the certification of service globally at "page 3", which is not true of any form I read.
whatContradictsTheRepository.where: data/rcap-grade-a/packet-factory-24h/SOURCE_RELATIONSHIP_REGISTRY.json canonicalArtifactTitle for "Certification of Service by Mailing or Delivery"
whatContradictsTheRepository.detail: The recorded locator is "Embedded certification section; current Rule 2.86 Form 2 example appears on page 3". On Form 4 and Form 5, opened here, the section is on page 2 of 2. Form 1's acquisition observed 3 pages and Form 3's observed 2, so the page number is a property of each containing form, not of the label.
whatContradictsTheRepository.whyThisMatters: It is the same error labelIsFamilySpecific exists to stop, one level down: a per-form locator recorded once, globally. A builder taking page 3 as the constant would map the section onto the wrong page of Forms 3, 4 and 5.
whatContradictsTheRepository.correctModel: Record the locator per containing form, or record none and let the read of each form supply it.

whatContradictsTheRepository.status: Already harmless in practice — the reconciler admits only confirmed_from_document_text… and this grade does not match — but it reads as settled to a human, and this return records that it is not.

recommendationsToCaptain: Regenerate SOURCE_RELATIONSHIP_REGISTRY.json against SOURCE_ACQUISITION_MANIFEST.json. Three of this lane's four documents are recorded as address-unknown in one file and address-settled-and-fetched in the other, and the registry is the file the dispatch tells lanes to read first.

Drop "Certification of Service by Mailing or Delivery" from the required-source list for all five Iowa families that name it. It is a section heading printed inside each family's own application. It is now the second Iowa label after the DCI pair to turn out to name no separate document.
Model DCI-76 and DCI-77 as one bundle with two components, so the census stops counting two blocked sources where one settled binary exists.
One page fetch of https://www.iowacourts.gov/collections/499/files closes the only genuinely open obligation in this lane and, with it, the last unaddressed source of ia-901c3-set.
whatFinishingThisDoesNotDo: Nothing here builds a packet, proves a packet or approves a route. Four addresses and a set of refusals are a better map of Iowa than the repository had this morning, and that is the whole of it.

claimLifecycle.whyReissued: All nine grants were released 2026-09-01T07:58 as collateral to the pass-1 lane-gate incident, without the obligations ever being worked. --reissue with a stated reason is the ledger's own mechanism for exactly this; the releases stay in ledger.releases and the reissues are appended to ledger.reissues.
claimLifecycle.whyStillLive: The contract says to release each COMPLETED obligation. These two are STOPPED, so they are not released. A live source-discovery grant blocks no acquisition lane — locate() scopes grants by laneKind — so holding them costs nothing and records honestly that the discovery work on Form 2 is unfinished. Releasing a grant on work that was not done is the exact mistake that put this lane here.
claimLifecycle.gateDisciplineFollowed: The reissues were committed BEFORE any evidence was read, so the lane gate saw a clean worktree and returned SOURCE_CONVEYOR_PREFLIGHT_READY. The lane gate and all nine row gates passed 2/2.
